questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose for personal reasons mainly. I had been to Korea before and wanted to go back. Also I am considering doing my graduate fieldwork in the region.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The whole experience was amazing. The only reason I am not choosing 10/10, is because of the lack of guidance mainly from KU.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough. I thought SNU were quite thorough with their explanations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of mails to read, and they had a few introductory events for all incoming students. I received a lot of help from the SNU buddy program as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got lucky. I contacted a few share houses that I found online. Only one answered. They had a room available and they let me reserve it without sending a deposit in advance. I lived with 11 Korean girls, but I had my own room and only shared a kitchen, living room and bathroom with 3 others. I thought it was quite comfortable and cheap (only around 3000 kr a month)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend living off campus! You get to see so much more and become familiar with 'normal' life (not just student life). I felt much more free living off campus as the rules were not as strict and I heard some unfortunate stories from the people living at the dorms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A little confusing at first, but reading through it a few times made it a lot more clear. I did not have a stressful time getting my courses as most of them were not that popular.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were given a guide and shown a video on how to do it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted. Most of them in the first round and two in the second round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Decide on the courses beforehand, add them to your 'wishlist', have plan B's and just click fast honestly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren't many Anthropology-courses in English, but I wanted to try out other subjects, so it worked out nicely for me.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were generally very easy, lower level than what I was used to. Only one course I took, which was a graduate course, was really on par with the academic level at KU. The other courses were not within my field, but I had no problem following them. I did not mind the level, as it gave me time to do other things.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Two of my courses had very little participation. It seemed like the professors didn't expect you to answer any questions at all. Three of my courses had a high level of participation though. Especially one of them was great, as it was more of a round-table discussion, which I thought very productive.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Studies in Korean Culture, Understanding Modern Culture, Two Koreas, Introduction to Film Art and 20th- and 21st- Century Fiction.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Studies in Korean Culture was great, but do not take it unless you are an anthropology or sociology student. Also I loved Understanding Modern Culture and Two Koreas, the latter being modern Korean history. The professors were both very engaging.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Mandatory health insurance. You can get an exemption, but it was not easy, so I ended up just paying it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I already knew the prices, but food and coffee is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of clubs. I didn't participate much, I did not feel like I had the time. Also some of the clubs were 'unofficially' not open to foreigners, as they did not want to speak English.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: SNU buddy program! If you put time into it, you will not regret it. I had an amazing group and it made all the difference.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get out and explore the city! There's so much to do and see. Definitely go hiking no matter if you've done it before or not. Go to Jeju in May or September.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have stayed in Korea for 3 months before, so it was no problem for me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again I would say SNU buddy and clubs. Or talk to some in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, but I might not be the best judge of that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Smart solutions for everything and how people generally are mindful of other people. I would say compared to Copenhagen people are a lot less loud (except when drunk), don't take up a lot of space and just are generally polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get involved with SNU buddy, be present in class even if the level is different from what you are used to (I learned a lot from hearing the perspectives of my classmates), also don't spend all your time with other Danes or travelling with friends or family from home (you can do that another time).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a climate card if you are staying off campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My classes, the SNU buddy program and travelling with the friends I made through both.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to go home haha

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
